feature1.prompt: Management command subparsers don’t retain error formatting. Django management commands use a subclass of argparse.ArgumentParser, CommandParser, that takes some extra arguments to improve error formatting. These arguments are not copied into subparsers, created via CommandParser.add_subparsers().add_parser(), resulting in stack traces on the CLI rather than human-facing usage messages. We can correct this by ensuring that the subparser action returned by add_subparsers() copies the relevant arguments through to constructed subparsers. For example, when a required subparser argument is missing, a proper usage message should be displayed instead of a traceback.
feature1.hint_texts: Feature 1 focuses on enhancing the core functionality of management commands. The change must be implemented in the add_subparsers method so that error formatting arguments are forwarded to subparsers. Developers should modify django/core/management/base.py to use functools.partial for wrapping the parser_class with the called_from_command_line attribute when necessary. The implementation must include a check using issubclass to determine if the parser_class inherits from CommandParser before applying the fix.
feature1.entrypoint: File to modify: django/core/management/base.py; Function: add_subparsers. Begin the changes near the existing error handling code and ensure the new partial wrapping is integrated appropriately for parser_class.

feature2.prompt: Management command subparsers don’t retain error formatting. Django management commands do not correctly copy extra error formatting arguments into subparsers, which causes missing required arguments to result in stacktraces instead of user-friendly error messages. The expected behavior is that subparsers display proper usage messages when errors occur, mirroring the behavior of the main command parser. This can be achieved by ensuring that the subparser action copies all relevant error formatting arguments when the subparser is constructed.
feature2.hint_texts: Feature 2 is dedicated to verifying the new behavior by adding automated tests. Developers should add new test cases that simulate the command line execution of commands with subparsers. The tests must check that a missing required argument shows a proper error message instead of a traceback, and that non-Django error formatting is handled correctly. Implementation should include writing and updating tests to cover both failure (before fix) and success (after fix) scenarios.
feature2.entrypoint: Files to update: tests/user_commands/management/commands/subparser_vanilla.py and tests/user_commands/tests.py. Focus on adding test functions such as test_subparser_error_formatting and test_subparser_non_django_error_formatting to validate the behavior of subparser error messages.

collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers implementing Feature 1 and Feature 2 need to coordinate regarding the expected error messages and argument propagation.
